chills.name: Chills
chills.bio: 37, a former gym owner who closed his gym four years ago to live on the road. He overlands the region out of his Porsche Cayenne with his cat Mutu — and a one-wheel electric skateboard strapped to the roof rack that he rides for fun. Climbs trees on a whim, just to sit up in the canopy and think. He preaches that nature heals the mind and that self-sustainable living is the cure for modern life. Calm, fit, genuinely capable in the wild — and endlessly optimistic, which the jungle is about to test.

memories.text: Wesley panicked and wasted water, but he's here and learning. That's enough.
Wesley admitted he couldn't start the fire and asked for help instead of quitting.
Wesley panicked and failed, but he stayed. He's still here. That matters.
He came forward wanting to work. That's the shift. That's real.
Wesley bent to real work without falling apart. That matters.
Wesley worked hard and didn't panic. He's stepping into something real.
Wesley didn't run. He stayed and did the work. That changes things.
Wesley's learning: patience wins in the jungle.
Wesley's trusting the slower way now. Real progress.
Wesley's learning to wait instead of force things.
Wesley's learning to trust the pace. That's the shift.
Wesley finally accepted his limits without panic or blame.
Wesley's accepting his limits without spiraling. That's real.

wesley.name: Wesley Koh
wesley.bio: 27, raised in Singapore's pressure-cooker — top schools, the scholarship track, a finance job — with wealthy parents and almost no time outdoors. He came on this trip only because his family was weighing whether to fund Chills' eco-retreat. Soft hands, anxious, fussy about discomfort — but genuinely book-smart (water chemistry, rationing, first aid). The jungle terrifies him; his mind is the only tool he trusts.

memories.text: Panicked over the cracked radiator and fouled the water. Day one.
Chills didn't blame me. He just said I'm learning. I want to believe that.
Chills showed me dry heartwood without blame when I'd already quit.
The fire caught. He wasn't preaching. He was saving us.
He didn't blame me like I feared. He just showed up ready.
I didn't panic. I just listened and did it. He trusted me.
Made it through a full day of work without breaking. Chills just noticed.
I worked all day without panicking. Chills saw it. That matters.
Slow heals faster than pushing through pain.
Patience isn't laziness. Chills was right. It's survival.
Resting is work too. Chills taught me that.
Chills didn't blame me for being broken. He just said tomorrow.
Chills didn't dismiss my pain. He said rest is the work.
Chills framed rest as the work I'm doing today. I'm starting to believe it.

mutu.name: Mutu
mutu.bio: Chills' ginger tabby — green-eyed, road-hardened from years of overlanding, and utterly unbothered. Independent and quietly devoted to Chills, a sly little hunter who senses the weather turning long before the humans do.
